statement.p: (a) Find a vector parallel to the line of intersection of the planes x - y - 2 z = 4 and 5 x - 5 y - 2 z = 12.
(b) Show that the point \left(1,-1,-1\right) lies on both planes. Then find a vector parametric equation for the line of intersection.

static.solution:
(a) Normal vectors to the two planes are \vec n_1 = \vec i - \vec j - 2 \vec k \quad \hbox{ and } \quad \vec n_2 = 5\vec i - 5 \vec j - 2 \vec k. The vector \vec n_1\times\vec n_2 is perpendicular to both planes and parallel to the line of intersection: \vec n_1\times\vec n_2 = \left| \begin{array}{ccc} \vec i \amp \vec j \amp \vec k\\ 1 \amp -1 \amp -2\\ 5 \amp -5 \amp -2 \end{array} \right| = -8\,\mathit{\vec i}-8\,\mathit{\vec j}.
(b) To check that the point \left(1,-1,-1\right) lies on the planes, substitute into each equation. x - y - 2 z = (1)(1) + (-1)(-1) + (-2)(-1) = 4, and 5 x - 5 y - 2 z = (5)(1) + (-5)(-1) + (-2)(-1) = 12. Thus, the point lies on both planes. Then a vector parametric equation of the line is \vec r(t) = \left(1-8t\right)\,\mathit{\vec i}-\left(1+8t\right)\,\mathit{\vec j}-\,\mathit{\vec k}.
